intro: 18 new Story Path stories, two for every feeling, so families who play every day don't keep meeting the same one. All drafts. Each picture's words are read aloud; at the choice the child picks what Smidgeon does, and either way ends back at still. Reply on each story: approve, or say what to change.

stories.title: The dancing leaves

beats.text: The wind blew, and the autumn leaves began to dance 🍂.
Smidgeon and Pip danced with them! Twirl, hop, twirl! He felt so happy 😄.
Faster, faster… whoops! He tumbled into the leaves, all dizzy 😵. He lay still for a moment.
He stood still and noticed: his heart was bouncy, his beak was smiling, his chest felt warm ☀️.
“This is what happy feels like!” he told Pip. “Mine too!” said Pip.
They sat in the leaves, happy and warm. Noticing happy helps you remember it 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you ever pause in a happy moment to notice it?
grownUp.insight: Children learn feelings through their bodies. Noticing a good feeling teaches them what to look for later.
grownUp.getLow: In a happy moment, ask: “Where do you feel happy in your body?”
thenSay: “You look so happy! Where do you feel it?”
“Let's remember this happy feeling.”

forChild: The leaves danced, and Smidgeon danced too 🍂.
He felt happy, with a warm chest and a big smile 😄.
He stopped to notice it: “This is what happy feels like!”

stories.title: Welcome home!

beats.text: Smidgeon waited at the nest. The grown-up had been gone all day 🪺.
Then… there they were! Smidgeon was SO happy he couldn't keep still 🥳!
He zoomed round and round the nest. Wheee! Then he landed, puffing. He still wanted to say hello 🪶.
He gave the grown-up a great big hug 🤗. “I'm so happy you're home!”
Then he told them all about his day, and they listened to every word 💬.
Big happy, said out loud, made both of them smile 💛.

grownUp.question: Do reunions at the end of the day feel rushed?
grownUp.insight: The moment you come back together is one of the biggest happy moments of a child's day.
grownUp.getLow: Give the first minute fully: get low, hug, and say “I'm so happy to see you.”
thenSay: “You're SO happy I'm home! Me too.”
“Tell me one thing about your day.”

forChild: The grown-up came home 🪺.
Smidgeon was SO happy 🥳.
He gave a big hug and said, “I'm so happy you're home!”

stories.title: The big race
stories.lesson: When excited makes it hard to wait

beats.text: The sparrows were having a race down the path 🏁.
“Can I race too?” Smidgeon was SO excited his feet were already running on the spot 🤩!
He zoomed off before anyone said go! “Come back, we have to start together!” 😅
He came back and stood still. One slow breath 🌬️. Ready… set…
“GO!” They raced down the path together, wings flapping 🏁!
Nobody minded who won. Excited is even more fun when you can wait for “go” 💛.

grownUp.question: Does excitement make it hard to wait their turn?
grownUp.insight: Excitement pushes the body to move now. One breath before the start teaches the body how to wait.
grownUp.getLow: Play “ready, set, breathe… go!” games at home: running, jumping, even stacking blocks.
thenSay: “You're SO excited to race!”
“Ready… set… breathe… go!”

forChild: The sparrows were having a race 🏁.
Smidgeon was SO excited his feet wouldn't wait 🤩.
He took one breath, waited for “go,” and raced with everyone.

stories.title: Story time

beats.text: Robin was telling a story under the big tree 📖.
It was about a dragon! Smidgeon had SO many ideas, his beak was bursting to talk 🤩.

choices.label: Hold it in a hug and wait

beats.text: “And then! And then!” Robin stopped. Nobody could hear the story 😕.
He hugged his wings round his idea and breathed 🌬️. He could hold it until the end.
“Any ideas?” asked Robin. “The dragon could breathe bubbles!” said Smidgeon.
Everyone loved it. His idea was even better when everyone could hear it 💛.

grownUp.question: Do they interrupt when they're excited?
grownUp.insight: Interrupting is excitement spilling over, not rudeness. Holding an idea is a skill they can practise.
grownUp.getLow: Teach a “hold it” signal: hands on heart means “I have an idea, I'm waiting.”
thenSay: “You've got a great idea! Hold it in your hands.”
“Now it's your turn. Tell us!”

forChild: Robin was telling a dragon story 📖.
Smidgeon had SO many ideas. That's a little excited 🤩.
He held his idea and waited his turn, and everyone loved it.

stories.title: The high branch

beats.text: Smidgeon looked up at the high branch. Every day he tried to fly up there 🌳.
Flap, flap, FLAP! Today he made it, all the way to the top! His chest puffed up 🌟.
He zoomed straight off to the next thing… and forgot to enjoy what he'd done. He flew back 🪶.
He stood tall and took a big, proud breath 🌬️. He'd practised SO many times.
“I practised and practised, and I did it!” he told the grown-up. “You never gave up,” they said.
From the high branch, he could see the whole park. Proud feels best when you stop to feel it 💛.

grownUp.question: Do they rush past their wins?
grownUp.insight: Pausing to feel proud helps a child connect effort with the good feeling, so they keep trying next time.
grownUp.getLow: After a win, pause together: “Stop and feel it. You did that.”
thenSay: “You did it! How does your body feel?”
“You practised so many times.”

forChild: Smidgeon practised flying to the high branch 🌳.
Today he made it! That's a lot of proud 🌟.
He stopped to feel it, then told the grown-up how he did it.

stories.title: The brave sorry
stories.lesson: Proud of doing the right thing

beats.text: Smidgeon zoomed around the playroom. Pip had built a tall block tower 🧱.
CRASH! His wing knocked it down by accident. Pip looked sad 😟. Smidgeon's tummy felt funny.
He tiptoed away, but the funny feeling followed him 😔. He went back.
“I'm sorry, Pip. I knocked it by accident. Can I help fix it?” 💛
They built it back together, even taller 🧱.
Smidgeon felt proud. Saying sorry was brave, and brave feels good 🌟.

grownUp.question: Do they hide mistakes because they're worried about being in trouble?
grownUp.insight: Owning a mistake takes courage. Noticing the courage (not just the mistake) makes it easier next time.
grownUp.getLow: When they own up, name the brave part first: “That was brave to tell me.”
thenSay: “That was brave, saying sorry.”
“How do you feel now?”

forChild: Smidgeon knocked down Pip's tower by accident 🧱.
He said sorry, and helped fix it 💛.
Saying sorry was brave. That's a little proud 🌟.

stories.title: Cloud watching

beats.text: Smidgeon had been running and running all morning 🏃.
“Let's lie down and watch the clouds,” said the grown-up ☁️.
He wiggled and chattered and couldn't see a single cloud shape. “Let's go slow,” said the grown-up.
He breathed slowly, in… and out 🌬️, and watched the sky drift by.
“That one looks like a fish!” “And that one's a sleepy bunny!” ☁️
His body felt slow and soft, like a cloud. Calm is lovely to share 😌.

grownUp.question: Is every minute of the day busy?
grownUp.insight: Children need slow moments to learn what calm feels like. Doing it together makes it feel safe, not boring.
grownUp.getLow: Try two minutes of cloud watching (or ceiling watching): lie down and name shapes together.
thenSay: “Let's go slow and look together.”
“How does your body feel now?”

forChild: Smidgeon had been busy all morning 🏃.
He lay down to watch the clouds ☁️.
Slow breaths, slow clouds: he felt calm 😌.

stories.title: Leaf boats

beats.text: By the pond was a big, still puddle. Wren showed Smidgeon how to make leaf boats 🍃.
Smidgeon grabbed a whole wing-full of leaves. He wanted them all on the water NOW!

choices.label: Throw them all in at once

beats.text: SPLASH! The leaves sank in a soggy clump 💦. “Let's try slowly,” said Wren.
He breathed out and set one leaf down, ever so gently 🍃. It floated!
They watched it drift across the still water, slow… slow… slow 🪷.
Smidgeon felt slow and quiet inside, like the pond. Going slowly helps calm come 😌.

grownUp.question: Is it hard for them to do things slowly?
grownUp.insight: Slow, careful movements calm the body, which is why rhythmic, gentle play settles children.
grownUp.getLow: Try a slow-motion game: pour water, stack cups or float leaves as slowly as you can.
thenSay: “Let's go slow… slower… slowest!”
“Look how calm the water is. How does your body feel?”

forChild: Wren showed Smidgeon leaf boats 🍃.
He set one down gently and watched it float 🪷.
Going slowly made him feel calm 😌.

stories.title: Jay's big squawk

beats.text: Smidgeon was resting high up in the oak tree. It was nice and quiet 🌳.
“SQUAWK!” Jay landed right beside him. Smidgeon jumped so high his feathers puffed out 😮!
“SQUAWK!” Now Jay jumped too 😲! Two jumpy birds. They needed a breath.
Smidgeon took a breath and looked 🌬️. It was only Jay, saying hello.
“Sorry I made you jump!” said Jay. They laughed and sat together. Surprises pass quickly with a breath 💛.

grownUp.question: Do they sometimes get cross after a fright?
grownUp.insight: A startle floods the body fast, and it can come out as anger. A breath gives the brain time to see it's safe.
grownUp.getLow: After a fright, help them look: “What was it? Oh, just Jay!”
thenSay: “That made you jump!”
“Let's take a breath and look.”

forChild: Jay landed with a big SQUAWK 🌳.
Smidgeon jumped! That's surprised 😮.
He took a breath, looked, and it was just Jay saying hello.

stories.title: The sudden rain

beats.text: The sun was shining in the meadow. Not a cloud in the sky ☀️.
Then… PLOP! A big raindrop landed on his head. And another! Rain, out of nowhere 🌧️!
He flapped and spun around. Now he was dizzy AND wet 😵. Time to stop and breathe.
He took a breath and looked around 🌬️. A big leaf! The perfect umbrella.
Wren hopped under too. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter. It sounded like music 🎶.
When the sun came back, they splashed in the puddles. Some surprises turn out fun 🌈.

grownUp.question: Do sudden changes throw the whole day off?
grownUp.insight: Surprises are hard because the brain had a different plan. A breath and a look help it make a new one.
grownUp.getLow: When plans change suddenly, say: “Surprise! Let's breathe and see what we can do.”
thenSay: “That was a surprise! The rain came so fast.”
“Let's take a breath. What can we do now?”

forChild: The sun was shining, then rain came out of nowhere 🌧️.
Smidgeon was so surprised 😮.
He breathed, found a leaf umbrella, and the rain turned into fun.

stories.title: The runaway ball
stories.lesson: When something won't go your way

beats.text: Smidgeon and Pip were kicking a ball in the meadow ⚽.
But every kick went the wrong way! His feathers puffed up, hot and grumbly 😣.
WHUMP! The ball flew far away, and Pip had to go and get it 😕. The grumbly feeling was still there.
He stopped. He breathed in… and out 🌬️. “This is tricky,” he said.
“Kick it softly, with the side of your foot,” said Pip. They tried together.
Tap! It rolled right to Pip. Tricky things get easier when you slow down 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you jump in to fix it when they get frustrated?
grownUp.insight: Frustration is the feeling of learning something hard. A pause and a little help teaches more than doing it for them.
grownUp.getLow: Name it first, then offer one small tip: “That's tricky. Want to try it softly?”
thenSay: “That's so tricky! You're frustrated.”
“Let's take a breath, then try one more time.”

forChild: Smidgeon's kicks kept going the wrong way ⚽.
He felt hot and grumbly. That's frustrated 😣.
He took a breath, Pip showed him a trick, and it worked!

stories.title: The wobbly pebbles

beats.text: Smidgeon wanted to make a perfect circle of pebbles 🪨.
They kept rolling out of place. “Stay THERE!” he huffed 😤.
He pushed them all over. Now there was no circle at all 😞. Maybe a break would help.
He sat with the grown-up and had a drink of water. Slowly, his feathers settled 🌬️.
Then he tried again, one pebble at a time, slowly… slowly…
A circle! Not perfect, but his. A break helped him come back to still 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you push them to keep going when they're about to explode?
grownUp.insight: A short break isn't giving up. It lets the body cool so the thinking brain can come back.
grownUp.getLow: Offer a break out loud: “Let's take a break and come back to it.”
thenSay: “Those pebbles are being tricky.”
“Let's take a break, then try again together.”

forChild: Smidgeon's pebbles kept rolling away 🪨.
He felt huffy. That's a little frustrated 😤.
He took a break, came back, and made his circle.

stories.title: The first splash

beats.text: The sparrows were splashing in the fountain. Splish, splash, SPLOOSH ⛲!
Smidgeon had never been in. His tummy felt wobbly, and his feet wouldn't move 😟.
He hid. “It's okay to feel nervous,” said the grown-up softly. “I'm right here.”
He held the grown-up's wing and took a slow breath 🌬️. “Just one toe?”
Dip. The water was cool and tickly! His wobbly feeling got a little smaller 💧.
One toe, then two feet, then a splash! Brave can be very small steps 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you say “there's nothing to be scared of”?
grownUp.insight: Nervous is real, even when the thing is safe. Feeling believed helps a child take the next small step.
grownUp.getLow: Stay close and shrink the step: “Just one toe. I'm right here.”
thenSay: “It's new, and new can feel wobbly.”
“Hold my hand. Just one little step.”

forChild: Smidgeon had never splashed in the fountain ⛲.
His tummy felt wobbly. That's nervous 😟.
He held the grown-up's wing and tried one toe, then splashed!

stories.title: The rumbly thunder
stories.lesson: When a loud noise feels scary

beats.text: Rain pattered on the leaves. Pitter, patter 🌧️.
BOOM! Thunder rumbled across the sky ⛈️. Smidgeon shook all over. His heart went thump, thump, thump!
He hid under a leaf, all alone. It was still very scary 😰. He wanted someone close.
He snuggled up close. “That was loud,” said the grown-up. “You're safe with me.”
They breathed together and counted the rumbles: one… two… they got further away 🌬️.
Soon it was just soft rain again. Someone close makes scary feel smaller 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you hurry to say “it's only thunder”?
grownUp.insight: A loud noise sets off the body's alarm before the brain can think. Closeness and a slow breath turn the alarm down.
grownUp.getLow: Get close first, words second: “That was loud. You're safe. Let's breathe together.”
thenSay: “That was SO loud! Your body got a fright.”
“I'm right here. Let's count the rumbles.”

forChild: Thunder went BOOM ⛈️.
Smidgeon shook all over. That's SO much nervous 😰.
He snuggled up close and breathed with the grown-up until it passed.

stories.title: Goodbye, Robin

beats.text: Robin was Smidgeon's friend. They built little pebble walls together every day 🪨.
“I'm going to visit my grandma, far away, for a long time,” said Robin. Smidgeon's wings drooped 😢.
“Whatever,” he said, and looked away. But the sad stayed stuck inside, heavy and lumpy 😔.
“I'll miss you,” he said, and gave Robin a big hug 🤗. A tear rolled down. That was okay.
Robin waved goodbye. “I'll come back, and I'll tell you everything!” 👋
That night, the grown-up held him close. Missing someone means you love them 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you try to cheer them up quickly when they're sad?
grownUp.insight: Sadness passes faster when it's allowed. Saying the true thing (“I'll miss you”) lets it move through.
grownUp.getLow: Let them be sad with you: “You'll miss Robin. Me too. Let's sit together.”
thenSay: “You're sad Robin is going away.”
“Missing someone means you love them.”

forChild: Robin had to go away for a long time 🪨.
Smidgeon's wings drooped. That's sad 😢.
He said, “I'll miss you,” and gave Robin a hug.

stories.title: Pip can't play

beats.text: Today Pip was coming to play! Smidgeon got his ball ready ⚽.
“Pip has a sniffly cold and needs to rest,” said the grown-up. Smidgeon's head hung low 😞.
He sat alone in a corner. Being alone made the sad feel bigger 😔.
“I'm sad,” he said. “I wanted to play with Pip.” The grown-up sat close. “That's disappointing.” 💛
Later, they rolled the ball together. It wasn't the same, but it was nice ⚽.
Pip would play another day. Sad things can still have nice moments too 🌅.

grownUp.question: Do you rush to a new plan the moment one falls through?
grownUp.insight: Disappointment needs a moment to be felt before the next plan can feel good.
grownUp.getLow: Name it first (“That's disappointing”), wait, then offer something small.
thenSay: “You were so looking forward to it.”
“It's okay to feel sad. Want to sit with me?”

forChild: Pip was sick and couldn't come to play.
Smidgeon's head hung low. That's a little sad 😞.
He said, “I'm sad,” and the grown-up sat with him.

stories.title: Jay's ruffle

beats.text: Smidgeon sat on his branch, feathers neat and smooth 🌿.
Then Jay swooped down and ruffled his feathers, all messy. Again, and again! Smidgeon's face went hot 😠.

choices.label: Yell as loud as he can

beats.text: “STOP IT!” he screeched. Jay jumped. Now everyone was upset 😬. Yelling made it bigger.
Stomp. Stomp. Stomp 🦶. Then a big dragon breath out 🐉. His steam came down.
“Stop. I don't like that,” said Smidgeon, in a strong, calm voice. Jay looked down. “Sorry.”
Jay sat nicely beside him. Angry is okay. Strong, calm words worked better than yelling 💛.

grownUp.question: Do you tell them “just ignore it” when someone keeps bugging them?
grownUp.insight: Being bothered on purpose makes anyone angry. The skill isn't hiding it; it's cooling the body, then using strong words.
grownUp.getLow: Teach one sentence: “Stop. I don't like that.” Practise it together when everyone's calm.
thenSay: “Jay kept ruffling you! Of course you're angry.”
“Let's stomp it out, then say ‘Stop, I don't like that.’”

forChild: Jay kept ruffling Smidgeon's feathers 🌿.
His face went hot. That's angry 😠.
Three stomps, a dragon breath, then strong words: “Stop. I don't like that.”

stories.title: Not time to go!

beats.text: Smidgeon was having the BEST time playing ball ⚽.
“Time to go home,” said the grown-up. “NO!” Smidgeon shouted. His whole body went hot and stompy 🌋.
He threw the ball. The grown-up stayed calm. “You're SO angry. I'm here.”
Breathe in big… and blow it out like a dragon 🐉. Again. And again. The volcano got smaller.
“I'm angry. I wanted more time,” said Smidgeon. “That makes sense,” said the grown-up. “One more kick, then home.”
One more kick, then home to the nest. Big angry can come down, breath by breath 💛.

grownUp.question: Do transitions turn into battles at your house?
grownUp.insight: Stopping something fun is a real loss for a young child. Anger is how the loss comes out.
grownUp.getLow: Warn before the end (“two more minutes”), name the feeling, then give one last turn.
thenSay: “You don't want to stop. You're SO angry.”
“Dragon breaths with me. Then one more kick.”

forChild: Smidgeon was having so much fun ⚽.
Then it was time to go, and he got SO angry 🌋.
Dragon breaths helped, then he said why: “I wanted more time.”
